pages.en: One special Friday Yusuf's father gets dressed before a flicker of light brightens the sky. He pulls on his heavy weatherproof jacket and the green woolen cap that covers his ears. He waves his boy goodbye. Yusuf's eyes brighten when Papa says, "Today is the day I will catch a fish and bring a gift home for you."

pages.zh: 一个特别的星期五，天还没亮，优素福的爸爸就穿好防风雨厚外套，戴上盖住耳朵的绿毛线帽，向孩子挥手。爸爸答应今天去捕鱼，还会带礼物回来，优素福眼睛一亮。
pages.tip: 先听故事，指指爸爸准备出海的衣帽。

pages.en: A fish and a gift? Oh, what will it be? Papa cycles down to Muizenberg Beach. Squeak squeak go the wheels all the way to Surfer's Corner. Gulls circle the sky. "Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?" they cry. "What will you bring back for Yusuf?" Papa rings his bell. "Wait and see what it will be!"

pages.zh: 一条鱼，一份礼物，会是什么呢？爸爸骑车去梅森堡海滩，车轮一路吱呀响。海鸥在天上盘旋叫着，像在问带什么给优素福。爸爸按铃回答：“等着看吧！”
pages.tip: 指指海鸥，轻轻演一演它的叫声。

pages.en: The fishermen watch the sun rise. They check their nets. They check their oars. They listen to the wind. They drag their boats down to the water. Yusuf's grandfather, Oupa Salie was a treknet fisherman. Before him his father, Oupagrootjie Ridwaan, knew the sea too.

pages.zh: 渔民看日出，检查渔网和船桨，听风声，把船拖入海。优素福的爷爷萨利是拖网渔民，更早的曾祖父里德万也熟悉这片海。
pages.tip: 找一找船桨和渔网。

pages.en: The boat rides into the waves. Papa's arms stretch to the oar. His leg braces against the side. His neck strains, his back muscles ripple. Papa sings as he works: "Drop and swish. Find a fish. Pull and plop. Don't you stop."

pages.zh: 船驶入波浪，爸爸伸臂划桨，腿抵住船边，脖子绷紧，背部肌肉起伏，边干活边唱：放下、划动，寻找鱼；拉起、落下，不停歇。
pages.tip: 用手臂轻轻演一演划船。

pages.en: All day long Yusuf looks at the sky. It is bright and clear and windless. A fish and a gift! What will Papa bring home from the sea? Sometimes he brings a beautiful shell. Sometimes he brings a jewel green bottle rinsed by the waves.

pages.zh: 优素福整天看着晴朗无风的天空，盼着鱼和礼物。爸爸有时带漂亮贝壳，有时带被海浪洗净、像宝石般绿色的瓶子。
pages.tip: 猜猜今天会带什么礼物，不必猜对。
pages.alt: 优素福整天看着晴朗无风的天空，盼着鱼和礼物。爸爸有时带漂亮贝壳，有时带被海浪洗净、像宝石般绿色的瓶子。

pages.en: Some days Yusuf's father brings a story. Like the time they found sea turtles on the sand, hundreds washed up in a storm. "Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?" cried the gulls. "What will you do to help the turtles?" Papa said, "We saved those turtles, I tell you straight. We sent them back to the ocean, every last one."

pages.zh: 有时爸爸带回来一个故事，比如有次风暴把数百只海龟冲上沙滩。海鸥叫着，仿佛问怎么办。爸爸说，他们救了海龟，把每一只都送回海里。
pages.tip: 指指海龟，听 turtles。

pages.en: Always Papa brings a song. He sings the song while he pulls the oars. He sings the song while he pulls the nets. He sings the song as he winds the ropes. He sings the song as he cycles home. "Drop and swish. Find a fish. Pull and plop. Don't you stop."

pages.zh: 爸爸总带着一首歌，划桨、拉网、盘绳、骑车回家时都唱：放下、划动，寻找鱼；拉起、落下，不停歇。
pages.tip: 听听反复出现的节奏，用手轻轻打拍。
pages.alt: 爸爸总带着一首歌，划桨、拉网、盘绳、骑车回家时都唱：放下、划动，寻找鱼；拉起、落下，不停歇。

pages.en: Ouma Safiya wants a nice fat yellowtail for her supper. Mother wants a new dress. "Don't be silly," says Ouma. "You'll be lucky if they catch even a tiny crab. More likely it will be fish tail Friday. There's not so many fish left in the sea." Yusuf holds Ouma's hand. They cross the road at the bathing cabins. "Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?" cry the gulls perched on the bright rooftops. "What is for supper?"

pages.zh: 萨菲娅奶奶想吃肥美的黄尾鱼，妈妈想要新裙子。奶奶说海里的鱼不多了，能抓到小螃蟹都算幸运，也许只有鱼尾巴。优素福牵着奶奶过马路，海鸥在彩色屋顶叫着，像在问晚饭吃什么。
pages.tip: 找找奶奶和孩子，先听懂他们在等待。

pages.en: Last year the fishermen fought with the surfers. Angry fists and shouting words. "Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?" cried the gulls. "There's enough sea for everybody," said Yusuf's father. He showed them the fishing license that had been Oupa Salie's. "Waves for all. Water for free."

pages.zh: 去年渔民和冲浪者曾争吵冲突。爸爸拿出祖传的捕鱼许可证，说海足够大家共享：“海浪给大家，海水自由流。”
pages.tip: 可以说：大家需要商量着共享海边。

pages.en: Ouma Safiya watches through her binoculars, her fingers curled in curiosity. The shark siren sounds. Swimmers run back to the sand and grab their towels. Surfers rush to the shore, carrying their boards under their arms. Under the showers they strip off their wetsuits. "Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?" cry the gulls. "What will Yusuf's father bring from the ocean?"

pages.zh: 奶奶用望远镜好奇地看。鲨鱼警报响了，游泳者拿毛巾跑回沙滩，冲浪者抱板上岸、冲水脱潜水衣。海鸥又叫，爸爸会从海里带回什么呢？
pages.tip: 指指岸边的人，说说听到警报要听从工作人员。

pages.en: Yusuf's father and uncle and cousins heave and pull. A little shark has been caught. It twists and thrashes in the waves. Yusuf's father untangles the nets, singing to the shark: "Drop and swish. Find a fish. Pull and plop. Don't you stop." When the shark at last is free it streaks back into the waves, leaving only one fat yellowtail in the net. Ouma Safiya will be pleased.

pages.zh: 爸爸和亲人用力拉网，一条小鲨鱼在浪里挣扎。爸爸解开网，唱着熟悉的歌。鲨鱼终于自由游回海里，网里只留一条肥黄尾鱼，奶奶会开心。
pages.tip: 找找游走的鲨鱼，看看爸爸怎样帮助它。

pages.en: The men pull the boat in and coil up the cables. A hard white triangle catches Papa's finger. "Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?" cry the gulls. "What did you bring back for Yusuf?" As the sun goes down, Papa answers the gulls. "A lucky shark tooth for my boy." At home Yusuf holds his gift up to the stars.

pages.zh: 男人们收船盘绳，一个坚硬的白色三角碰到爸爸手指。海鸥仿佛追问礼物，夕阳下爸爸回答：“给孩子一颗幸运的鲨鱼牙。”回到家，优素福举起礼物，望向星空。
pages.tip: 指指礼物，回想最开始爸爸的承诺。

activity.title: 画一份来自海边的礼物
activity.text: 画一片海浪、一只海龟或一个想象中的贝壳送给家人。去海边时不惊扰动物，也不带走活物。
activity.hint: 想玩就试试；指图、用中文说或只听故事都可以。

zh: 姆基泽先生的四分之一面包

pages.en: It is nearly break time at Siyafunda Primary School. The two spaza shop owners at the school are preparing lunch to sell to hungry children.
pages.sourceText: It is nearly break time at Siyafunda Primary School. The two spaza shop owners at the school are preparing lunch to sell to hungry children.
pages.zh: 西亚丰达小学快到休息时间，两位校内小店主正准备午餐，卖给饥饿的孩子们。
pages.tip: 先找到故事里的两家小店。
pages.alt: 西亚丰达小学快到休息时间，两位校内小店主正准备午餐，卖给饥饿的孩子们。

pages.en: In Mr Motaung's shop, the bread is cut and ready for making kotas. He carefully cuts out the soft middle of each quarter loaf. Then he puts polony and chips in the space inside. Motaung puts two spoonfuls of his wife's homemade atchar in each kota. He likes to boast that his kotas have atchar inside and atchar on top!

Motaung puts two spoonfuls of his wife's homemade atchar in each kota. He likes to boast that his kotas have atchar inside and atchar on top!
pages.zh: 莫陶恩先生把面包切成四分之一块，挖出软芯，放入午餐肉和薯条，再加两勺妻子做的酸辣腌菜。他得意地说，面包里面和上面都有腌菜！
pages.tip: 看看面包里夹了什么。
pages.alt: 莫陶恩先生把面包切成四分之一块，挖出软芯，放入午餐肉和薯条，再加两勺妻子做的酸辣腌菜。他得意地说，面包里面和上面都有腌菜！

pages.en: In Mr Mkhize's shop, the chips are nearly ready, but he is still cutting his bread for kotas. He is worried because things are not going well with his shop. "It started well," thinks Mkhize. "But now I get fewer and fewer customers. At least I'm reducing some of my costs by cutting five kotas from a loaf."

pages.zh: 姆基泽先生的薯条快好了，还在切面包。他担心顾客越来越少，却想把一条面包切成五块，至少能省些成本。
pages.tip: 先看切开的面包，猜猜大小会怎样变化。

pages.en: Jabu and Zodwa are buying lunch. Zodwa buys from Mr Mkhize. Jabu buys from Mr Motaung. He believes that Motaung's kota has got more chips and atchar than Mkhize's kota.
pages.sourceText: Jabu and Zodwa are buying lunch. Zodwa buys from Mr Mkhize. Jabu buys from Mr Motaung. He believes that Motaung's kota has got more chips and atchar than Mkhize's kota.
pages.zh: 贾布和佐德瓦买午餐，佐德瓦去姆基泽家，贾布去莫陶恩家，他觉得那里夹的薯条和腌菜更多。
pages.tip: 找找两位孩子买的面包。

pages.en: The queue at Mr Motaung's shop is always longer. Zodwa waits for Jabu. Then the friends sit together in the shade to enjoy their kotas.

pages.zh: 莫陶恩店前的队总更长。佐德瓦等着贾布，两人再到树荫下坐着吃。
pages.tip: 指指队伍，看看哪边人更多。
pages.alt: 莫陶恩店前的队总更长。佐德瓦等着贾布，两人再到树荫下坐着吃。

pages.en: Zodwa notices something that makes her stare and frown."What are you staring at?" asks Jabu."Your kota! It looks bigger than mine," says Zodwa.
pages.sourceText: Zodwa notices something that makes her stare and frown."What are you staring at?" asks Jabu."Your kota! It looks bigger than mine," says Zodwa.
pages.zh: 佐德瓦盯着贾布的面包皱眉，觉得他的比自己的大。
pages.tip: 比较两块面包的样子，不用量尺寸。
pages.alt: 佐德瓦盯着贾布的面包皱眉，觉得他的比自己的大。

pages.en: They both look very closely at their kotas. Sure enough, Jabu's is bigger. "Something is not right here," says Zodwa. "I wonder if this is the reason Mr Mkhize's shop is not busy anymore." Jabu thinks for a while and then he replies, "Well, I heard that some kids saw Mkhize cutting his bread into five pieces for kotas!"

Jabu thinks for a while and then he replies, "Well, I heard that some kids saw Mkhize cutting his bread into five pieces for kotas!"
pages.zh: 两人仔细看，贾布的果然更大。佐德瓦怀疑这和姆基泽生意变差有关，贾布说听说他把一条面包切成五份。
pages.tip: 回想一开始说好的是什么份量。

pages.en: Nomsa overhears Jabu and Zodwa talking and she's curious. She asks them what's wrong with cutting the loaf into five pieces for kotas. Zodwa and Jabu reply together, "A kota is a quarter of a loaf!" Nomsa still looks confused, so Zodwa explains, "The loaf must be cut into four equal pieces. Otherwise, they are not quarters."

pages.zh: 诺姆萨听了好奇，问切五份有什么错。两人解释：kota 指四分之一，整条必须切成四块同样大小的，才叫四分之一。
pages.tip: 听 equal，用中文说“一样大”。

pages.en: Nomsa is cross because she also buys from Mr Mkhize. "So, he is stealing bread from us!" she says in a loud voice. Zodwa decides to go back to Mkhize's shop to complain. She marches off, holding her kota up in the air. Nomsa hurries behind her. Hungry Jabu looks longingly at his kota and sighs. Then he gets up to follow his friends.

pages.en: I live in Kakuma village, a very hot dry place, full of thorny trees, and more goats than people. Even the market place is quiet, with only a few small shops. Most people use bicycles for transport.
pages.sourceText: I live in Kakuma village, a very hot dry place, full of thorny trees, and more goats than people. Even the market place is quiet, with only a few small shops. Most people use bicycles for transport.
pages.zh: 我住在卡库马村，那里炎热干燥，长着带刺的树，山羊比人还多。市场也很安静，只有几家小店，大家大多骑自行车出行。
pages.tip: 看看村庄的交通和商店。

pages.en: One morning my mother called me and said, "Etabo, today you turn six years old. We have a present for you." "What is it? What is it?" I asked eagerly. "Tomorrow we're going by bus to the market in Eldoret," she replied, "And we're taking you with us!" My first visit to the city! I was so excited that I could hardly sleep that night.

pages.tip: 说说第一次去新地方是什么心情。

pages.en: The next day at the Kakuma bus stop, I stood between my mother and my aunt in my new pair of blue jeans and red T-shirt. I felt very small between my tall slender mother and my big round aunt.

pages.en: A long time ago, in the vast city of Johannesburg, a baby girl was born. That baby was me. My mom called me Miriam. Miriam Makeba.

pages.zh: 很久以前，在大城市约翰内斯堡，一个女婴出生了，那就是我。妈妈给我取名米丽娅姆·马凯巴。

pages.en: Mom was a sangoma, but she also worked to make other people's homes neat and clean. It was hard for my mom to earn enough for both of us. She started selling homemade beer to bring in more money.

pages.en: The laws of the land said that selling homemade beer was wrong. The police sent my mom to jail for six long months. I was only 18 days old, and needed my mom. So even though I was just a baby, I went to jail too.

pages.en: As a little girl I loved to sing. When I was older, I helped my mom clean houses. Singing songs as I worked made the chores go faster and the days seem brighter. Singing made me happier than I can explain.

pages.en: I sang in my church, and this made others happy too. Music has the power to bring people together. When we were singing we felt brave and strong.

pages.en: My home was Sophiatown, a place of culture and music. Sophiatown, a place where South Africans could make music in harmony and dance together. But the people who ruled the land at the time did not like this togetherness. Those rulers didn't want black and white people to be friends.
pages.sourceText: My home was Sophiatown, a place of culture and music. Sophiatown, a place where South Africans could make music in harmony and dance together. But the people who ruled the land at the time did not like this togetherness. Those rulers didn't want black and white people to be friends.
pages.zh: 我的家在索菲亚镇，一个充满文化和音乐的地方，人们一起奏乐跳舞。但当时的统治者不喜欢这样的团结，不想让黑人和白人成为朋友。
pages.tip: 说一句：不该因为肤色不同就阻止人交朋友。

pages.en: I knew it was wrong to treat people differently because of their skin colour. I did not hide my beliefs, and so those people in charge wanted me out of the country. When I was singing in America, I was told I could never return home.

pages.zh: 我知道按肤色区别对待人是不对的，也不隐藏想法，当权者因此想把我赶走。我在美国演唱时，被告知再也不能回家。
pages.tip: 看看她的表情，先听她的经历。

pages.en: People all over the world heard my story. My songs and my story helped many to see how there was no fairness in South Africa for those with black skin. I decided to go on singing and telling the truth about my country, no matter what.
pages.sourceText: People all over the world heard my story. My songs and my story helped many to see how there was no fairness in South Africa for those with black skin. I decided to go on singing and telling the truth about my country, no matter what.
pages.zh: 世界各地的人听见我的故事，我的歌让更多人知道南非黑人受到不公平待遇。我决定无论怎样，都继续唱，讲述祖国的真相。
pages.tip: 可以说：讲出经历，能让更多人了解。
pages.alt: 世界各地的人听见我的故事，我的歌让更多人知道南非黑人受到不公平待遇。我决定无论怎样，都继续唱，讲述祖国的真相。

pages.en: The world loved my music and I was welcomed in many countries. I won awards and sang for important people all over the globe. My life was good, but something was missing. I could not sing in my home country, and people there were not free.
pages.sourceText: The world loved my music and I was welcomed in many countries. I won awards and sang for important people all over the globe. My life was good, but something was missing. I could not sing in my home country, and people there were not free.
pages.zh: 大家喜欢我的音乐，许多国家欢迎我。我获得奖项，为许多人演唱，生活虽好，却少了一样：不能在家乡唱歌，那里的人也还不自由。
pages.tip: 说说她最想回到哪里。

pages.en: Then a wonderful day dawned when Nelson Mandela became president of South Africa. New people were in charge and the unfair laws belonged to the past. I finally went home with new hope in my heart.

pages.zh: 终于，纳尔逊·曼德拉成为南非总统，不公平的旧法律过去了。我怀着新的希望，回到家乡。

pages.en: After that I could sing in a free, fair country. People of different skin colours could enjoy music together. I helped make this happen because I was brave and strong. I sang the truth in all of my songs.

pages.zh: 此后，我能在自由、公平的国家唱歌，不同肤色的人一起享受音乐。我因勇敢、坚持而帮助促成改变，把真相唱进每首歌。

activity.title: 一起唱一小句
activity.text: 和家人轻轻唱一段熟悉的旋律，或拍手打节奏。每个人都可以选择自己舒服的声音。

pages.en: Long, long ago, the Sky God, Nyame, kept all stories locked in a wooden box, high in the sky. People down on earth had no stories to tell and they were very sad. They asked Anansi the clever Spider to help them.
pages.sourceText: Long, long ago, the Sky God, Nyame, kept all stories locked in a wooden box, high in the sky. People down on earth had no stories to tell and they were very sad. They asked Anansi the clever Spider to help them.
pages.zh: 很久以前，天神尼亚梅把所有故事锁在天上的木箱里。地上的人没故事可讲，很难过，便请聪明的蜘蛛阿南西帮忙。
pages.tip: 先看木箱，听 stories。

pages.en: Anansi spun a long thread, and climbed up his sticky thread all the way to heaven. "Can I have the stories, please?" he asked the Sky God. But Nyame laughed at Anansi and said, "Oh, these are very expensive stories. You wouldn't be able to pay for them, little spider."

pages.zh: 阿南西吐出长丝，沿着黏丝爬到天上，请求得到故事。尼亚梅笑它，说故事太贵，小蜘蛛买不起。
pages.tip: 用手指演一演向上爬。

pages.en: "How much do the stories cost?" asked Anansi. "You'll have to bring me three rare and fierce animals," Nyame answered, "A leopard with sharp teeth like spears, a hornet that stings people, and a snake that swallows people whole." He laughed and laughed. He thought his stories were quite safe.

He laughed and laughed. He thought his stories were quite safe.
pages.zh: 阿南西问价钱。天神要三种罕见凶猛的动物：利齿像矛的花豹、会蜇人的大黄蜂，以及能整个吞人的蛇。他大笑，觉得故事安全了。
pages.tip: 说明这是夸张的民间童话，只需认出三种动物。

pages.en: So Anansi climbed slowly back down his sticky thread to the earth. He thought and he thought, and he came up with a plan. He dug a deep hole, covered it with branches and dirt so it was hidden, and he went home for supper. In the morning, sure enough, a leopard had fallen into his pit. He was furiously scratching at the side of the pit, but he couldn't get out.

He dug a deep hole, covered it with branches and dirt so it was hidden, and he went home for supper. In the morning, sure enough, a leopard had fallen into his pit. He was furiously scratching at the side of the pit, but he couldn't get out.
pages.zh: 阿南西回地上想出办法，挖深坑，用树枝泥土盖住，自己回家吃饭。第二天，花豹果然落入坑里，愤怒地抓挠，却出不来。
pages.tip: 找找坑里的花豹，不模仿做陷阱。
pages.alt: 阿南西回地上想出办法，挖深坑，用树枝泥土盖住，自己回家吃饭。第二天，花豹果然落入坑里，愤怒地抓挠，却出不来。

pages.en: "Oh let me help you, my dear friend!" said Anansi. "Just lie down on these sticks and I'll pull you out." Anansi wound his sticky web round the leopard and the sticks, and pulled him up to heaven to show the Sky God. But Nyame just laughed and said, "Where are the other two?"

pages.zh: 阿南西假装帮忙，让花豹躺在木棍上，再用蛛丝绑好，拉到天上给天神看。天神仍笑着问其他两种在哪。
pages.tip: 用简单中文说：第一个任务完成了。

pages.en: So Anansi went back down to earth to get the second creature. He thought and he thought and he came up with a plan. He took a gourd full of water and went to the tree where the hornets lived. He poured out some of the water all over their nest. Then he cut a leaf from a banana tree and held it over his head, and he poured the rest of the water all over himself.

pages.zh: 蜘蛛回地上想第二个办法，带一葫芦水到蜂巢，先往巢上倒水，再把香蕉叶顶在头上，将剩余的水倒到身上。
pages.tip: 看看它怎样假装下雨，不接触真实蜂巢。

pages.en: He called out to the hornets, "Hey hornets! Come see! It is raining! Quick - get inside my gourd and it will keep all of you dry." Hornets don't like to get wet, so they all flew into Anansi's gourd.

pages.zh: 它喊黄蜂来看，说下雨了，快躲到葫芦里避雨。黄蜂不想淋湿，就全飞进去了。

pages.en: Then Anansi quickly spun a web across the opening so the hornets couldn't get out no matter how much they buzzed. He carried them up to heaven and showed them to the Sky God. But Nyame just said, "Where's the last one?" (He wasn't laughing so much anymore.)

pages.zh: 蜘蛛迅速用网封住开口，黄蜂嗡嗡叫也出不来。它把黄蜂送上天，天神问最后一个在哪，这次没那么得意了。

pages.en: So Anansi went down to earth again. He thought and thought and he thought, but he couldn't come up with a plan. So he asked his wife, who had a very good idea. Together they found a good long thick branch and some strong vines. When they got near the stream where the snake lived, they began to argue. "The branch is longer!" "No, it isn't!" "Yes it is!"

Together they found a good long thick branch and some strong vines. When they got near the stream where the snake lived, they began to argue. "The branch is longer!" "No, it isn't!" "Yes it is!"
pages.zh: 蜘蛛又回地上，想来想去没办法，便问妻子。妻子有了主意，两人找到粗长树枝和藤蔓，到蛇住的溪流旁，故意争论树枝是不是更长。
pages.tip: 说说遇到难题也可以请别人一起想。

pages.en: Soon the snake came out and asked what the argument was. "I was arguing with my wife," said Anansi. "She says this stick is longer than you are. But I don't agree." "Of course I'm longer than that stick!" said the snake. "I'm very long! I'm a huge snake! Just put your stick next to me and measure!"

pages.en: So Anansi did that, and he tied the snake to the stick with his vine to keep him straight. When he was all tied up, Anansi took the snake up to heaven.

pages.en: Nyame had to admit that Anansi had paid his price. So he went to his wooden box, opened the lid, and gave all the stories to Anansi. Anansi carried the stories triumphantly down to earth. He shared them with his wife, and with all the other animals and people. Stories are for telling, not for keeping in wooden boxes.
